title: ÆTHER: Fine-u Dhaan Di (quirky Tamil indie-pop breakup song, 1 min)
story: A Chennai guy gets dumped by text on a Monday morning and insists to everyone (and to a teasing female voice) that he is totally fine. He dances it off, then the twist: he accidentally likes her new photo.

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 18:49: 'new one Radhima like track'. Reference: Radhimaa (Aug 2026), a peppy, quirky Tamil indie-pop breakup song. Traits only (music.md s13 indie-pop profile, no names in prompts): bouncy piano motif, rubbery bass, jazzy sevenths, light mridangam/tabla under a pop kick, mandolin and brass layered in, deadpan male lead with a teasing female voice answering, about 100 BPM. Original melody and lyrics, nothing copied. Raga: Mohanam (D major pentatonic), Sa D. Avoided shared devices: 3-note call, hey chants, whistle, nadaswaram/thavil, 808 drop, reversed swell.

positive_styles: playful, quirky modern Tamil indie-pop breakup song, a funny 'I am totally fine' denial song, peppy and feel-good, a big singalong
D major pentatonic melody (D E F# A B only, no G, no C), raga-shaped with quick slides, bends and little turns on the vocal and the lead
one steady 100 BPM bouncy groove from start to end, laid-back swing in the hi-hats, a cheeky triplet pickup at section ends

layered indie-pop production: a simple bouncy piano motif, a warm rubbery bass groove, jazzy seventh chords, a pop kick and snap, light dry mridangam and tabla patterns underneath, mandolin and a small brass section added one by one
nostalgic retro South Indian colour inside a modern clean mix
a deadpan, cheeky young male voice singing in Tamil with clear diction, half-sung half-talked verses, playful English words
a sweet, teasing young female voice answering his lines with short sung replies
real instruments close and natural, no heavy echo
warm, bright, punchy mix
starts with the piano motif and a phone notification ping, bass and snap join by 3 s, he speaks the line flat and deadpan
